cards.text: Here in Isaiah, the LORD speaks, and He starts BIG: 'Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool.' Friend, my whole planet is just big enough for one bakery, and God puts His FEET up on the earth.
Then He asks, 'What kind of house will you build for Me? Or where will My place of repose be?' That's like handing the ocean a bucket and saying, 'Here, move in.'

cards.question: Right after asking about a house, the LORD asks another question. True or false: He says His own hand made all these things.
The LORD made all these things, and then He names the one He will esteem. Who is it?

answers.text: The humble one who trembles at His word
The one who brings the grandest offerings
The one with the most famous name

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about people bringing offerings. Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man, and whoever sacrifices a lamb is like one who breaks a dog's neck.
Whoever presents a grain offering is like one who offers pig's blood, and whoever offers frankincense is like one who blesses an idol. Friend, that is a hard list to hear.

cards.question: These people ARE bringing offerings. What does the LORD say about them?

answers.text: They have chosen their own ways
They offer on the wrong days

cards.question: These people have chosen their own ways. So the LORD says He will ___ their punishment.
The LORD says He will bring terror upon these people. True or false: It's because they brought Him no offerings.

cards.text: Why the terror? The LORD says, 'I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.' That's calling somebody over and over and getting voicemail EVERY single time.

cards.question: Now the word of the LORD goes out to a different group. Who is called to hear it?

answers.text: Those who tremble at His word
Those who serve in the temple

cards.text: Their own brothers hate them and exclude them because of the LORD's name. That's not getting left out of the group chat, friend, that's your own family REMOVING you from it.

cards.question: Those brothers say, 'Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!' But the LORD says they will be put to ___.
Then comes a shout: an uproar from the city and a voice from the temple! Whose voice is it?

cards.text: It's the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve. And THAT is one call nobody gets to send to voicemail.
Then the LORD paints a picture: 'Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before she was in pain, she delivered a boy.' That's like your package landing on the porch before you even clicked 'Buy.'

cards.question: After that birth, the LORD asks about it. True or false: He says people hear about things like this all the time.

cards.text: Then He asks, 'Can a country be born in a day or a nation be delivered in an instant?' Friend, I can't get ONE batch of cookies done in an instant, and He's talking about a whole NATION.

cards.question: The LORD answers His own question about a nation born in a day: Yet as soon as ___ was in labor, she gave birth to her children.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, 'Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?' And then, 'Or will I who deliver close the womb?'

cards.question: The LORD asks if He would bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it. What's He saying with that question?

answers.text: He needs more time to decide
He leaves the rest to someone else

cards.text: He finishes what He starts, friend, which is more than I can say for the half-sprinkled batch sitting on my counter right now. Then the call goes out: be glad for Jerusalem and rejoice over her, all who love her.

cards.question: The call to rejoice over Jerusalem keeps going. True or false: Even those who mourn over her are told to rejoice greatly with her.

cards.text: And the picture is a nursing mother: those who love Jerusalem will nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts, and delight in her glorious abundance.
Then the LORD says He will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of nations like a flowing stream. Not a drip, not a trickle, friend, a RIVER.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, those who love Jerusalem are like little ones with her. What happens to them?

answers.text: They are carried on her arm
They are sent off to her fields
They are left outside her gates

cards.question: Jerusalem has been the nursing mother in this picture. Now the LORD says He Himself will comfort those who love her. Like who?
Comforted by the LORD like a son by his mother, those He comforts will be consoled over ___.

cards.text: And here's the promise: when you see, you will rejoice and flourish like grass. You mow grass on Saturday, and by Wednesday it's back and laughing at you.

cards.question: Then the hand of the LORD will be revealed. True or false: His wrath will be shown to His servants.

cards.text: His hand will be revealed to His servants, and His wrath will be shown to His enemies. Friend, I know which side of that line I want to be baking on.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word in 'I will choose their punishment' (Isaiah 66:4) before they have seen it. The meaning (the LORD will punish them) could just as easily be 'bring' or 'send'. The baker can only land on 'choose' by ruling out 'delay' and 'lighten', or by spotting the wordplay with 'chosen their own ways'. So it tests wording, not meaning. Ask about the meaning instead, or tell the 'choose' echo on a story card.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Isaiah 66:11 says 'so that you may nurse and be satisfied... you may drink deeply and delight yourselves.' The card turns this into a firm 'will nurse... and delight,' and it drops the 'so that' link back to the call to rejoice in 66:10. That states as certain what the cited verses give as a purpose ('may'). Keep the verse's 'so that... may' wording.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
